findings.message: The diff changes plugin code in specclaw-review, specclaw-sync (new bin and tests) and specclaw (specclaw-pr), but it bumps no `plugin.json` (claude or codex) and no `marketplace.json` entry. Every plugin must ship at the same version, and a code change with no bump at all is a major. Bump all `plugins/*/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, all `plugins/*/.codex-plugin/plugin.json` and every `plugins[]` entry in `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` to one new identical version.
findings.scenario: Release this branch: the installed specclaw-sync, specclaw-review and specclaw plugins keep the old version string, so users never receive the new `release` command, the `--head` verdict or the status posting.

findings.message: `release_gate.block_on` is parsed twice: `Config.block_on` in review_core.py and `block_on()` in specclaw-sync. The two copies disagree on an empty list. review_core keeps `[]` because `isinstance(v, list)` wins, so nothing blocks. specclaw-sync falls back to DEFAULT_BLOCK_ON via `vals or DEFAULT_BLOCK_ON`. They also parse the YAML differently (quote stripping, block lists). Use one implementation, or have the sync tool call the review parser. Add a table test that runs both over the same config variants.
findings.scenario: Config has `release_gate:\n  block_on: []`. The fast track treats a security blocker as deferrable debt and the round exits 0. `specclaw-sync release` then falls back to law/security/data-loss, lists the same item as BLOCK and exits 1. The two gates give different verdicts for one config. The test suites cover neither the empty list nor any cross-check between the two parsers.

findings.message: `verdict_at` requires the final round's recorded `head` to equal the PR head exactly. The documented flow (SKILL step 5) commits the round records after the final pass and then pushes. A round file cannot contain the SHA of the commit that adds it, so the PR head always differs from the recorded `head`. The tests confirm this: after the 'records' commit, plain verdict is OK and `--head` exits 1. The CI templates also derive CHANGE from round files committed in the PR. In the normal commit-records-then-PR flow the `specclaw/review-loop` status is therefore never posted. Make the gate accept a head whose diff from the recorded head touches only `.specclaw` records, or record a tree/content hash that excludes the records. Otherwise document that the status only works when the records are left uncommitted.
findings.scenario: Run the final pass at commit A → `git add .specclaw && git commit` creates B → `/specclaw:pr` pushes B. `specclaw-review verdict --head B` exits 1 with 'final pass A is not head B', so `post_review_status` posts nothing. Branch policy requiring the status can never be satisfied.

findings.message: `normalise_class` maps a missing or unrecognised `class` to `other`, which is never gate-blocking. A model that omits the class on a real security blocker lets it go to `debt.md` under the fast track. `specclaw-sync release` then passes it. Flag a blocker or major with no valid class (for example keep it blocking, or mark it `unclassified`) instead of defaulting to the permissive class.
findings.scenario: Fast track on; the backend returns `{"severity":"blocker","message":"sql injection","scenario":"..."}` with no class → class `other` → round exits 0, item written to debt, release exits 0.
